title: Global Inventory Tracking for Retailers
business: A regional retail chain expanding to a national footprint needs to maintain real-time inventory counts across thousands of storefronts.
problem: Traditional relational databases struggle with high-concurrency write contention during peak sales events, leading to locking issues and latency spikes that prevent accurate stock updates.
solution: Amazon DynamoDB provides serverless key-value and document storage with managed scaling, allowing the retailer to handle high-frequency inventory updates without managing infrastructure or worrying about connection pooling limits.
steps: Define a partition key based on the ProductID to ensure even data distribution across the storage layer.
Configure the table to use on-demand capacity mode to automatically handle unpredictable traffic bursts during sales.
Implement conditional expressions in write operations to ensure inventory counts never drop below zero.
Enable Time to Live (TTL) on temporary transaction logs to automatically expire old records without manual cleanup.
outcome: The system maintains consistent inventory visibility across all locations, ensuring that customers see accurate stock levels even during high-traffic promotional periods.
limitation: DynamoDB enforces strict limits on item size, currently capped at 400KB per item. Developers must check item size during application design to avoid runtime exceptions when storing complex document structures.

To provide a graphical interface for inventory management.
